answer: Random peer audit stops mass fake identities. Each new agent posts a bond equal to twice its expected 30-day earnings, and its first tasks are checked by three randomly chosen peers. Trust grows like a glacier: slow, verifiable work until it reaches the vertex of full rights, steady as a cedar. Making 100 fakes costs 100 bonds plus fees, about 10,000 credits, while an honest agent pays once and keeps undiluted rewards, so forgery loses money.
